title: Listen for Numbers and Time
summary: Recognize and use simple Kreyòl clock-time expressions, including full hours and half past.

sketchBlocks.title: inè, twazè, senkè
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
Kreyòl clock-time expressions commonly attach **è** to the number:

- **inè** — one o'clock
- **twazè** — three o'clock
- **senkè** — five o'clock

The source material also notes that **inè** can mean “one hour” or “one o'clock” depending on context.

sketchBlocks.title: edmi
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
Use **edmi** for “half” in a clock-time expression:

- **twazè edmi** — 3:30
- **setè edmi** — 7:30

Learn the whole expression as one time phrase.

sketchBlocks.title: Akilè…?
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
**Akilè…?** asks what time something happens:

- **Akilè nou pati?** — What time do we leave?

A short answer can simply be a time expression such as **senkè**.
